report.summary: Claude's default mode moves from bypassPermissions to auto in every place that sets it: spec 01 Agents table, the server default (queue.ts), the web plan toggle (agents.ts), the Mac plan toggle (chat_model.rs), and the conformance harness and README. The tests that check it are updated. The new turn-summary rule in protocol is word for word the same as spec 01, and the workspace-events tests use the constant, so they follow it. The implementation note matches the code: the evidence lists auto, and tempod logs a failed mode change and keeps the current mode. Nothing is blocking; three small gaps remain.

findings.text: No Mac test checks the Claude branch of plan_target. The existing tests cover only Codex and Pi, so nothing checks that leaving plan mode as Claude returns to "auto". Rule 14 asks for a test for changed behavior; consider adding a Claude case next to the Codex one at about line 1541.

The implementation note cites this file as proof that auto is supported. The file is marked "live": false and still records setMode: "bypassPermissions", so no live run has yet shown that setting auto succeeds. A conformance run with the updated harness should refresh this evidence.

The pass criterion for spike S3 still requires the modes to include bypassPermissions. docs/01 line 104 still explains that IS_SANDBOX=1 exists so bypassPermissions is shown. Both may need a review now that auto is the default. They are still true as written, so this is not blocking.
